title: Publish the Open-Source & Civic Tech Fellowship Sprint Operating Blueprint for Impact Foundations, by Fri 18 Dec
description:
Global and pan-African technology foundations sponsor 3-month open-source and civic-tech fellowships (pairing junior contributors with senior maintainers on public infrastructure). Fellowship leads struggle to coordinate contributor standups, pull-request code reviews, and stipend milestone verification across disparate platforms. This blueprint turns Zedu into a dedicated fellowship sprint headquarters.

Work under this goal:
- Architect the multi-project fellowship channel hierarchy: open contribution project rooms (#civic-health-app, #public-data-portal), maintainer office-hour spaces (#maintainer-sos), and weekly showcase channels.
- Author the bi-weekly 30-minute contributor sprint planning and PR triage protocol using native Zedu Buzz screen-sharing sessions.
- Establish the pull-request review and milestone demo thread guidelines utilizing Zedu's 440px discussion drawer to document code critique and issue resolution.
- Design the fellowship milestone proof and stipend verification folder structure in Zedu File Management with secure view permissions for grant auditors.

Done when: A turnkey fellowship operations guide is published with contributor onboarding checklists, maintainer triage scripts, PR discussion templates, and grant audit compliance workflows verified against production zedu-fe controls.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Check whether Zedu connects to GitHub before designing PR reviews around it, and give a manual weekly PR roll-call if it doesn't
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Fellowship sprints live in GitHub pull requests. Approach: verify in the current product and docs whether Zedu has any GitHub integration or webhook. If yes, design the per-project PR feed; if not, write a manual weekly roll-call template (each fellow posts PRs opened, reviewed and merged, with links) in a thread per project, and a stipend-milestone checklist that links to merged PRs as evidence. Done: the integration finding with sources, the roll-call and milestone templates, and the channel layout for one sample fellowship.

upvotes.reason: "Check whether Zedu connects to GitHub before designing PR reviews around it, and give a manual weekly PR roll-call if it doesn't" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

This avoids promising a GitHub connection that may not exist and still gives fellowship teams a practical manual PR check if it does not. It includes source verification, ready-to-use templates and a sample channel layout, so the work can be completed either way.
Checking whether Zedu has a GitHub integration before designing PR feeds prevents a blueprint built on a feature that does not exist, with a manual fallback if it does not.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
Designing PR reviews around an integration that may not exist wastes the blueprint. Verifying the GitHub connection first, with a manual roll-call fallback, is the correct order.

pendingIdeas.title: Pay stipend milestones on evidenced merged work, not standup attendance
pendingIdeas.description: The milestone folders need a rule for what counts as proof. Approach: require each milestone submission to link the merged pull requests, name the maintainer who reviewed them, and attach a two-minute demo or a test log; an auditor checks each link and records sign-off in a small contribution ledger (who wrote, who reviewed, who merged). Done: a ledger template, a milestone evidence checklist, and one worked example with placeholders. Measured: every milestone has a named reviewer sign-off and a working link, and zero attendance-only milestone approvals in the first sprint. Why it fits: the goal pairs junior fellows with maintainers on public infrastructure, and grant auditors need proof that the stipend bought merged work rather than meetings.

upvotes.reason: Tying grant stipends directly to auditable git commits and merged pull requests aligns incentives around actual deliverable code rather than passive presence.

Paying on merged pull requests with a named reviewer and a ledger turns a vague milestone into evidence someone can audit. It also removes the incentive to attend standups and ship nothing, which is exactly the failure mode of stipend programmes.
Directly tackles a verified acquisition or conversion friction point with clear, evidence-based scope.
